thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Quality degradation alert scoped to tenant=acme-corp on dedicated-pool-7 (model=rwd-chat-7b-q4_1_fast). Eval-hook breach: 58% fail rate. Paging oncall.

Nina (SRE): I'm taking this. Marta, what's the customer-facing symptom?

Marta (Support): acme-corp reported increased wrong-entity substitutions in their batch inference (ticket ACME-454). They say it started after a config push during the 16:20 maintenance window.

Ethan (Ops): deployment audit shows a tenant-targeted config push at 16:19:44 UTC: quant_profile set to `q4_1_fast` for tenant acme-corp. The push was marked successful by the control-plane.

Yara (ML Infra): that profile is the new aggressive quantization we tested for throughput. It removes per-layer scale guards to squeeze memory. It can under certain structured-prompt regimes cause token instability.

Ibrahim (Runtime): mitigation choices: 1) control-plane rollback of the tenant key (fast); 2) runtime-level override to force `rwd-chat-7b-fp16` for all requests from acme-corp (slightly slower but safer); 3) apply request-level confidence clamp that throws higher-confidence thresholds back to customer (less intrusive). Fastest is 1.

Nina (SRE): perform the rollback. Also please capture ack counts from runtime.

Yara (ML Infra): executing rollback command now:
```
redwoodctl tenant-config update --tenant acme-corp --key quant_profile --value q4_0_stable --apply
```

deploy-bot: change initiated by Yara; id change_20260314_acme_03

Ethan (Ops): control-plane reports propagation to the dedicated pool; nodes acked: 6/6.

Ibrahim (Runtime): runtime telemetry shows eval-hook pass rate improving within 30s. Pre-rollback probe: pass 42%; post-rollback probe: pass 90% (n=50). I'll keep the runtime fallback rule ready if re-apply happens.

Marta (Support): acme-corp: "Most outputs look normal now, thanks. We'll continue tests on edge cases and report if anything odd."

Yara (ML Infra): preliminary trace: `q4_1_fast` pruned KV padding and used per-layer folding that under long chemical notation prefixes can shift positional alignment. Repro on internal harness with acme test corpus.

Nina (SRE): created incident INC-2026-0314-ACME-03. Owners: Nina (lead), Yara (ml root cause), Ibrahim (runtime), Ethan (ops), Kai (customer comms).

Kai (CSM): I'll draft an immediate customer note: "We reverted a quantization change applied to your dedicated pool; expected remediation window was under 2 minutes. We're conducting a full review and will share a postmortem and mitigation plan." Will send once postmortem is ready.

Ibrahim (Runtime): added a temporary runtime guard: block tenant-scoped quant updates that are not accompanied by a canary metric pass flag. Patch ref: RUNTIME-8801. If control-plane tries to apply `q4_1_fast` for acme again, runtime will reject and log.

Yara (ML Infra): opening a PR to add an optional KV-padding knob and to run the acme corpus through every quant profile before rollout. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/qprofiles/pull/1102

Nina (SRE): timeline snippets for postmortem record:
```
2026-03-14T16:19:44Z control-plane apply quant_profile=q4_1_fast tenant=acme-corp
2026-03-14T16:22:05Z eval_fail_rate=58% probe=50
2026-03-14T16:23:10Z change=change_20260314_acme_03 revert_to=q4_0_stable runtime_ack=6/6
2026-03-14T16:23:45Z eval_fail_rate=9% probe=50
```

Marta (Support): acme-corp asked that we do not re-run aggressive quant profiles on their pool without explicit opt-in. Logging that preference in the tenant record.

Ethan (Ops): I'll add a pipeline guard to the rollout service to require a metrics gate for tenant-scoped rollouts. Ticket: DEPLOY-4164.

Kai (CSM): forwarding this to the account team and legal as requested by acme.

Nina (SRE): handing off monitoring to Ethan for the next 3 hours. If it stays stable, we'll transition to postmortem cadence. Closing the live mitigation thread; follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-0314-ACME-03. :white_check_mark:
